$note: Authorized deviations for spexr (Tier A, delivered, IDE). Each entry cites the design-language.md rule that blesses it and states the scope of the grant. An entry without a justifying rule is a defect in disguise. spexr's tuned indigo accent family is NOT here — it lives in accent-registry.json (it is the product's registered accent, allowlisted by the audit).

deviations.why: design-language.md L3: code-content runs mirror the editor font; design-layer labels use --sl-font-code. Deliberate split, not a violation.

design-language.md §Decision 1 (IDE substrate): the agent panel and code editor are product-specific surfaces the DS grammar does not define role tokens for. spexr pins them per theme in spexr-overrides.css. SCOPE: blesses the property NAME, so any value assigned to it in any [data-sl-theme] block is accepted — these are product role tokens, not brand accents. --sl-agent-rail is intentionally absent: it holds the indigo accent, already allowlisted via accent-registry.json.

Dead-code fallback for the --sl-status-danger token: every occurrence is var(--sl-status-danger, #e5484d) in Theia chrome, and the DS theme layer always sets --sl-status-danger, so the literal never renders. Radix red, theme-agnostic. Blessed by exact value (no distinctive selector — it recurs across error pills/cards/rows).

Theia vendor-chrome fallback: var(--theia-widget-border, rgba(128,128,128,0.25)) on the smart-search progress track. Theia always sets --theia-widget-border, so the neutral grey never renders. Blessed by value — a vendor integration fallback, theme-agnostic.

design-language.md §Decision 2 (on-arbitrary-surface text): near-black ink placed on a categorical --cat-color chip background (.spexr-smart-search__filter-chip--active), so it stays readable on whatever bright hue the category resolves to — the same pattern as daos's on-ink status pair. Blessed by value.
